clue.text: Foxtrot in a cracking guitar arrangement, one having its roots in Barbados

definitions.text: one having its roots in Barbados

indicators.note: cracking says that small group breaks open the shuffled guitar and sits inside it
an arrangement of the word guitar puts its letters in a new order
in says the foxtrot letter goes inside the word for 'a'

parts.note: a means per, as in 'ten pounds a day'
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A guitarist works a foxtrot into an arrangement of a tune from the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a sneaky one: it means 'per', as in a price per day. 'in' builds PEFR, 'arrangement' gives GRAUIT, and 'cracking' opens that up around PEFR.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus fruit is thought to have first arisen in Barbados in the eighteenth century, as a chance hybrid of pomelo and orange.

clue.text: Nativity plays avoiding sex and self-love

indicators.note: plays says the remaining letters move about freely, as in a rearrangement
avoiding says those letters are left out of the word Nativity

parts.note: IT is a long-standing slang word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: School nativity plays steer clear of sex and vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes IT from NATIVITY, leaving NAVITY; 'plays' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanity is excessive pride in oneself and one's looks, a kind of self-admiration or conceit.

clue.text: Philosopher's insincere talk being broadcast

indicators.note: being broadcast says the word is heard spoken, not read on the page

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, pious talk

explanation.surface: A philosopher's empty talk goes out over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was the eighteenth-century German thinker behind the Critique of Pure Reason.

clue.text: Family member invites one cutting meat

indicators.note: invites means the sibling takes in the cutter, holding it within

parts.note: a sib is a sibling, a brother or sister
a parer is someone or something that pares, trimming or cutting away

explanation.surface: A relative asks a carver over to cut up the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: This cut of pork from the ribs, with most of the meat trimmed off, is a common barbecue and Chinese-takeaway dish.

clue.text: Food price

definitions.meaning: food served, as in 'simple country cooking'
the cost of a ticket for a journey by bus, train or taxi

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the meals on offer and the charge a passenger pays to travel.

clue.text: Vehicle gets through blustery rain — sheer delight!

indicators.note: gets through says the vehicle pushes its way into the middle of the weather word
blustery weather is wild and gusty, so the letters of rain are blown about

parts.note: a van is a kind of vehicle

explanation.surface: A van battles through a squall, and arriving is pure bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism it is the state of perfect peace; loosely, any state of perfect happiness or bliss.

clue.text: Piece of music to some extent in one tempo

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A composition is played partly at a single, steady speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition written for nine instruments or voices, as a quartet is for four.

clue.text: Perhaps the 20th strategy works

parts.note: a plan is a strategy
T is the twentieth letter of the alphabet, one example of a 20th

explanation.surface: A twentieth-century strategy, perhaps, that actually works.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in the answer in the order PLAN then T. 'works' is the noun, as in 'gasworks'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial site or factory, the same sense as works in 'steelworks'.

clue.text: Cost, insurance and freight wind up business

indicators.note: up, in a down entry, says the letters read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: CIF is the shipping term for cost, insurance and freight
fart is slang for breaking wind

explanation.surface: Shipping charges finish off a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CIFFART round. 'wind up' looks like a phrasal verb meaning to close a company, but the two words do different jobs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means trade or dealings, often illicit, as in drug traffic.

clue.text: Party claiming independence is a steal

indicators.note: claiming means the party takes hold of the letter, keeping it within

parts.note: the SNP is the Scottish National Party
I is a standard abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: A Scottish party demanding independence is called a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the SNP campaigns for Scottish independence.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a bargain, a purchase so cheap it feels like stealing.

clue.text: Complicated triangle with Queen coming in between Kings

indicators.note: coming in says the queen's letters go into the middle of the rearranged word
complicated says the letters of triangle are muddled into a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: A tangled love triangle as a queen comes between two kings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complicated' gives INTREGAL, and 'coming in' splits it after INT; 'between Kings' is a rare adjective, the period between reigns.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the gap between two reigns, as in an interregnum when a throne stands empty.

clue.text: Get lost in poorly-ventilated institute of education

parts.note: a stuffy room lacks fresh air
the OU is the Open University, a British distance-learning university

explanation.surface: Someone loses their way in a badly aired college building.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude British dismissal, much like telling someone to go away or clear off.

clue.text: Almost certain to break up — that's appropriate

indicators.note: to break says the word up is split open with the shortened word inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost says the word for certain loses its final letter

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: It's nearly certain a couple will split, and rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like the adjective 'suitable' but is the verb, to take for oneself; 'Almost' and 'to break' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize a power or position wrongfully is to take it over without right, as a pretender takes a throne.

clue.text: City closed in by raging fire — this one in Brazil?

indicators.note: closed in by says the city letters are surrounded by the rearranged fire
a raging fire is wild, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A city is hemmed in by a blaze, perhaps somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' does double duty: it supplies letters, and 'this one' in the definition points back to it. 'raging' gives RIFE, and 'closed in by' places the city after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Recife is a large port on Brazil's north-east coast, capital of Pernambuco state.

clue.text: Association's argument against foreign tourism

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and different, so the letters of tourism are rearranged

explanation.surface: A group objects to tourism from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A consortium is a partnership of companies or bodies formed for a joint venture.

clue.text: Jacob's relative's appeal to split European Union

indicators.note: to split says the appeal letters break the union apart, sitting inside it

parts.note: SA is sex appeal

explanation.surface: A relative of Jacob urges a break-up of the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this hairy hunter was Jacob's twin brother, who sold his birthright for a bowl of stew.

clue.text: Dogs got surrounded by pigs

indicators.note: surrounded by says the word for got sits inside the pigs

parts.note: sows are female pigs
had means got, as in 'had a cold'

explanation.surface: Some dogs have been encircled by a herd of pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogs' looks like the animals but is the verb, to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them doggedly, the way a detective tails a suspect.

clue.text: Firework: possibly 25 are missing, one British

indicators.note: missing says the letters of are are taken away from the number word

parts.note: 25 is five times five, an example of a square number
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A firework that has lost 25 of its parts, one being British.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but here it is just the number. 'missing' takes ARE from SQUARE, leaving SQU.
explanation.definitionFit: A squib is a small firework that fizzes before exploding, as in 'damp squib'.

clue.text: State in which Pierre is welcoming coffee bar on deserted oil platform

indicators.note: is welcoming means the state takes in the following pieces as guests, holding them inside

parts.note: Pierre is the capital of South Dakota, abbreviated SD

indicators.note: on, in a down entry, says the cafe word sits above the next piece

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe

indicators.note: deserted means emptied, so the word oil loses its insides and keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Somewhere a Frenchman called Pierre lets a coffee shop open on an abandoned oil rig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pierre' looks like a Frenchman, but it is the capital of South Dakota.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised platform, for builders or for an execution.

clue.text: Pretty new diamonds

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A lovely new set of diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean pleasant or attractive, as in a pleasing, likeable picture.

clue.text: Words frequently repeated by attractive woman lacking power

indicators.note: lacking says the power letter is removed from the woman

parts.note: a mantrap is slang for a seductive woman
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An attractive woman, losing her power, keeps saying the same words.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a phrase or sound chanted over and over in meditation, or a slogan said again and again.

clue.text: Pressure to pass the ball to a team mate? Succeeded in decisive matches

parts.words: to pass the ball to a team mate?
parts.note: to lay off is a football term for a short pass to a teammate; the question mark flags the definition by description
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: A coach urges passing to colleagues, and the team wins the deciding games.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra games arranged to settle a championship, a tie or promotion, are deciding contests.

clue.text: A troubled Ezra Pound's not one keeping body and soul together

definitions.text: not one keeping body and soul together

indicators.note: troubled suggests disorder, so the letters of Ezra are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A troubled Ezra Pound is no one who holds life together.
explanation.walkthrough: Ezra Pound looks like the American poet, but the two words split; 'troubled' gives ZRAE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish and Islamic tradition Azrael is the angel of death, who parts the soul from the body.

clue.text: Female winners at Wimbledon becoming well-known people

parts.note: an ace in tennis is a serve that wins the point outright; Wimbledon is the London tennis championship

explanation.surface: Women champions at Wimbledon turn into celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A face is a recognisable figure, as in 'famous faces' for celebrities.

clue.text: Great enthusiasm for redeveloping very old flea market

indicators.note: redeveloping says those letters are rebuilt in a different order

parts.note: a fair is a market or bazaar

explanation.surface: Someone is passionate about rebuilding an ancient flea market.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair can be an intense passion for a thing, as in 'his love affair with jazz'.

clue.text: Dead, gone to heaven (and elsewhere)

indicators.note: gone to heaven, in a down entry, says the word rises and reads bottom to top

parts.note: late means dead, as in 'the late king'

explanation.surface: Someone has died and gone to heaven, or perhaps somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead, gone to heaven' reads as a euphemism for death, but 'gone to heaven' sends LATE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation can stand for et alibi, 'and in other places', as well as et alii, 'and others'.

clue.text: Yes, German impressed by American guitar hero

indicators.note: impressed by says the German word is pressed into the guitar word

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of axe, slang for a guitar
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A German says yes, wowed by a US guitar legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guitar hero' looks like one phrase but splits between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a great Greek warrior at Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: College in Whitechapel

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the letters of the place name

explanation.surface: A college in the East London district of Whitechapel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tech is short for a technical college, an institute for practical training.

clue.text: Young pack animals going west bar one

indicators.note: bar means except, so a letter is left out
going west, in an across entry, says the word reads right to left

parts.note: llamas are used as pack animals in the Andes
A means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: Young pack animals head west, all but one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns LLAMAS into SAMALL, and 'bar' drops an A.
explanation.definitionFit: The young are little ones, as in 'small children'.

clue.text: Attenborough's original Planet Earth must be screened, one way and another

indicators.note: original means the very first letter of the name
must be screened says Earth is hidden within the planet, as behind a screen

parts.note: Venus is a planet

explanation.surface: David Attenborough's original Planet Earth series must be shown on TV in one form or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screened' looks like a TV broadcast, but it means hidden, putting E inside VENUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are routes or approaches, a way here and another way there, as in 'explore all avenues'.
